disease: MELAS (mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, stroke-like episodes; m.3243A>G in MT-TL1)
suspended_reason: The cause is a MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME (mtDNA) POINT MUTATION -- in ~80% of MELAS, m.3243A>G in MT-TL1, the gene encoding the mitochondrial transfer RNA for leucine, tRNA-Leu(UUR) (the remainder including m.3271T>C in the same tRNA and m.13513G>A in MT-ND5) -- NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. The three features that suspend LHON all apply, and a NEW one sharpens the point. (1) The lesion is in the ~16.6-kb circular MITOCHONDRIAL genome, transcribed as long POLYCISTRONIC transcripts from the mitochondrial heavy / light-strand promoters and then processed -- there is NO nuclear-style TSS -2000..+500 promoter window for MT-TL1 from which to read a gamma switch (the kit's data path resolves NUCLEAR RefSeq promoters; mtDNA genes have no such promoter). (2) Penetrance is HETEROPLASMY-dependent and tissue-variable -- the mutant load differs between tissues and over time, and (unlike a Mendelian switch) leukocyte heteroplasmy correlates poorly with clinical severity; the SAME m.3243A>G also produces a clinically DISTINCT maternally-inherited diabetes-and-deafness (MIDD) phenotype at lower loads -- a continuous, multi-outcome quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (3) Inheritance is MATERNAL (mitochondrial), not Mendelian. (4) THE NEW, SHARPER POINT vs LHON: MT-TL1 is a mitochondrial tRNA GENE, not a protein-coding subunit gene. Where LHON's suspended lesions sit in PROTEIN-CODING Complex I subunit genes (MT-ND4 / MT-ND1 / MT-ND6), the MELAS lesion disables a piece of the mitochondrial TRANSLATION machinery itself: the m.3243A>G tRNA-Leu(UUR) defect (loss of the wobble taurine modification / impaired aminoacylation / reduced tRNA-ribosome association) globally impairs synthesis of ALL thirteen mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS proteins -> Complex I deficiency -> energy failure in high-demand neurons and myocytes (stroke-like episodes, lactic acidosis, encephalomyopathy). So MELAS is the SECOND mtDNA suspend and it GENERALISES the mitochondrial-genome hold ACROSS mtDNA GENE CLASSES -- from a protein-coding subunit gene (LHON) to a mitochondrial tRNA gene (MELAS) -- the within-class generalisation analogue of how Beckwith-Wiedemann (11p15.5) generalised the IMPRINTING hold beyond Prader-Willi / Angelman's 15q11-q13: NOT a brand-new mechanism class, but proof the mtDNA hold keys on the MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME mechanism regardless of whether the mtDNA gene is protein-coding or a tRNA. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold). Like LHON, MELAS is suspended NOT for lack of any therapy but purely on engine-readability: management is supportive (the acute stroke-like episodes are treated with L-arginine; high-dose taurine -- aimed at restoring the missing tRNA wobble modification -- is approved for MELAS in Japan; CoQ10 / cofactor 'mito-cocktails' are used), and experimental approaches exist (allotopically expressed / mitochondrially-imported corrective tRNA; mitochondrially-targeted nucleases to shift heteroplasmy), but none is a single-(nuclear)-promoter switch the engine can read. An mtDNA / heteroplasmy / translation-defect model is future work, not a single-switch emergence. (Goto 1990 Nature 348:651, m.3243A>G in MELAS.)
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
